# HRD-W-0001

<!-- Generated by `mustur export`. Do not hand-edit: `mustur verify` fails on drift, and the store is the record. -->

**Group save sharing in the DevOfPie fork**

work-unit · 2026-09-13

repository: [MUS-R-0002](../routing.md#mus-r-0002)

## Context

Friends share one co-op world save (Valheim first) so any member can host when the others are offline, built into the DevOfPie fork of Hoard (why: HRD-I-0001).

Design, as shaped with Pie on 2026-09-13:
1. Game launch locks nothing. Hoard's GameStarted event (agent.rs:5424) arms: it pulls the latest copy of every shared world for that game.
2. One world is claimed. With one shared world for the game, ask Host / View / Not playing it. With several (across groups), a picker of worlds with their groups plus none of these. Only the chosen world is locked. Launch-time locking is rejected because it locks every shared world a player has.
3. File evidence verifies the claim. Open files: /proc/<pid>/fd on Linux and Proton (Hoard already reads it, agent.rs:4837); the Windows Restart Manager API on Windows, no driver (Hoard has a Windows lock probe, locks.rs). Writes are the late backstop (autosave, exit). Unverified: whether Valheim holds the world file open or reads it and closes it.
4. On a mismatch, a shared world the player did not claim being opened or written: if its lease is free, take it and tell the player; if someone else holds it, warn at once and keep that session's writes as a side copy, never pushed over the shared save.
5. Host takes a lease that renews on a heartbeat (model it on Hoard's presence: liveness derived from the last beat, devices.rs:31-59, presence.rs), pulls, and pushes and releases after the final flush on GameStopped (agent.rs:5483). A crash or power loss expires the lease.
6. View gets the latest copy and pushes nothing back; autosaves and the exit save are discarded or kept as a local-only snapshot. In Valheim loading a world runs a server, so a viewer can build and lose it: the prompt must say so, and several writes in a View session raise a warning. A viewer upgrades to Host only if the shared head has not moved since their copy.
7. Detection is after launch and there is no launch wrapper, so a lease can warn and hold sync back but cannot stop a second member launching.

What Hoard needs (evidence in .local/group-sharing/architecture-map.md in the checkout):
- Membership: saves are owned by one account, UNIQUE(user_id, game_slug, label), and every server query binds the caller. Needs a members table and authorization rewritten for shared saves.
- Blobs: dedup is per account by design (migrations/0013_blobs.sql:4, content existence never leaks across accounts). Shared saves need blobs keyed to the save owner or a group namespace.
- A lease table and routes (acquire, renew, release, force), wire types and golden fixtures, IPC requests and events, a kernel hold reason for locked by another member.
- World file scope: a save is a whole folder with no file subset (backup.rs:630-720). Valheim's world is <name>.db and <name>.fwl plus .old backups, and characters must stay out. Needs a per-game rule naming a world's files; the Ludusavi manifest only names folders. Interim: a world subfolder tracked as its own save with its own label.
- Merges are last writer wins by file mtime (kernel/restore_merge.rs), unsafe for a world database, which is what the lease prevents.
- Self-hosted SQLite and cloud Postgres are separate server stacks with separate migrations; build self-hosted first.

Decisions still open, for Pie through Mustur when the work reaches them: whether shared blobs may reveal content existence across accounts; who a shared save's storage and bandwidth count against (cloud); whether cloud support is attempted at all or left to the upstream maintainer; the lease TTL and heartbeat interval; how much per-game world-file mapping ships in the first version (Valheim only?); whether and when to offer the design to upstream (AGENTS.md there asks before code).
